title: Rounding and Estimation
seo_title: Estimation and Rounding – Primary 4 Mathematics Worksheets with Answers (NERDC)
standard_text: Round numbers to the nearest ten, hundred and thousand; estimate sums and differences by rounding. (summary of the NERDC Primary 4 Mathematics curriculum)
meta_desc: Free Primary 4 maths worksheets on rounding to the nearest ten, hundred, thousand and hundred thousand and estimating sums and differences. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Look at the digit to the right of the place.
body_html:
How to think about it

  • To round, look at the digit just to the right of the place you are rounding to.
  • If it is 5, 6, 7, 8 or 9, round up. If it is 0, 1, 2, 3 or 4, round down.
  • To estimate a sum or difference, round each number first, then add or subtract.

Examples

Example

Round 46,382 to the nearest thousand

The hundreds digit is 3

Answer: 46,000

Example

Estimate 4,872 + 3,214

5,000 + 3,000

Answer: about 8,000

Common mistakes

MistakeWhat to do instead
Looking at the wrong digitLook one place to the right.
Rounding 3,500 down5 rounds up: 4,000.
Not changing the digits after the place to 046,382 → 46,000.

faq.a: To check that an answer is sensible and to calculate quickly.

faq.q: Is an estimate the exact answer?
faq.a: No. It is close to the answer.

items.q: Round 6,685 to the nearest 1,000.
items.e: 6,685 is between 6,000 and 7,000. Look at the hundreds digit: 6. It is 5 or more, so round up. So 6,685 ≈ 7,000.

items.q: Round 4,500 to the nearest 1,000.
items.e: 4,500 is exactly halfway between 4,000 and 5,000. A number exactly halfway rounds up. So 4,500 ≈ 5,000.

items.e: 6,044 is between 6,000 and 7,000. Look at the hundreds digit: 0. It is 4 or less, so round down. So 6,044 ≈ 6,000.

items.e: 6,457 is between 6,000 and 7,000. Look at the hundreds digit: 4. It is 4 or less, so round down. Do not round in two steps (6,457 → 6,500 → 7,000). Round the number you started with. So 6,457 ≈ 6,000.

items.q: Round 9,615 to the nearest 1,000.
items.e: 9,615 is between 9,000 and 10,000. Look at the hundreds digit: 6. It is 5 or more, so round up. The thousands digit is 9, so rounding up makes 10 thousands. Rename 10 thousands as 1 ten thousand: 9,000 + 1,000 = 10,000. So 9,615 ≈ 10,000.

items.q: Which number rounds to 3,000 when you round it to the nearest 1,000?
items.e: Numbers from 2,500 to 3,499 round to 3,000. 2,684 is in that range. 3,500 rounds to 4,000.

items.e: 2,499 is between 2,000 and 3,000. Look at the hundreds digit: 4. It is 4 or less, so round down. Do not round in two steps (2,499 → 2,500 → 3,000). Round the number you started with. So 2,499 ≈ 2,000.

items.q: 99,600 ≈ ☐ when it is rounded to the nearest 1,000. What number goes in the box?
items.e: 99,600 is between 99,000 and 100,000. Look at the hundreds digit: 6. It is 5 or more, so round up. The thousands digit is 9, so rounding up makes 10 thousands. Rename 10 thousands as 1 ten thousand: 99,000 + 1,000 = 100,000. So 99,600 ≈ 100,000.

items.q: What is the smallest whole number that rounds to 8,000 when you round it to the nearest 1,000?
items.e: Numbers from 7,500 to 8,499 round to 8,000. 7,499 rounds down to 7,000, so the smallest is 7,500.

items.q: Round 6,348 to the nearest 10, the nearest 100 and the nearest 1,000. Which list is correct?
items.e: Always round the number you started with, 6,348. Nearest 10: the ones digit is 8, so 6,350. Nearest 100: the tens digit is 4, so 6,300. Nearest 1,000: the hundreds digit is 3, so 6,000. Do not round 6,350 again to get 6,400 and then 7,000.
